scope: Spring Boot 2.7.x to 3.0.x; normalize earlier 2.x through 2.7 first. Later 3.x minors are not certified by this catalog.

drifts.title: Trailing slash routes stop matching
drifts.old_behavior: An unpaired route also accepts its trailing-slash variant.
drifts.new_behavior: The extra slash requires an explicit route.
drifts.business_impact: Existing clients receive 404 on previously accepted URLs.

detection.summary: MVC/WebFlux dependency plus a literal mapping with an unpaired non-root path.
detection.limitations: Only literal annotation paths are parsed. Class-level prefixes, constants, composed annotations, router functions, proxies and actual client URLs require review. An explicit pair restores both paths in MVC and WebFlux.

fix.application: Add the slash variant to each flagged mapping. Preserve its existing method body, HTTP verb and authorization rules.
fix.caveat: Only literal annotation paths are parsed. Class-level prefixes, constants, composed annotations, router functions, proxies and actual client URLs require review. An explicit pair restores both paths in MVC and WebFlux.

sources.section: Spring MVC and WebFlux URL Matching Changes

verification.runtime: Boot 2.7.18: /api/greeting/ = 200; Boot 3.0.13 default: 404; exact catalog explicit-pair fix on the same URL: 200. Real Boot context / MockMvc; see evidence/boot27-maven.txt, evidence/boot30-contract-red.txt, evidence/boot30-restored-green.txt.

drifts.title: Default log timestamps change shape
drifts.old_behavior: Default timestamps separate date and time with a space.
drifts.new_behavior: Default timestamps use T and append an offset.
drifts.business_impact: Fixed-format log ingestion or alert parsing can silently lose events.

detection.summary: Boot logging path with no local timestamp/layout override.
detection.limitations: External LOG_DATEFORMAT_PATTERN, logging exclusions, JSON encoders and external logging files are unknown; inspect the real collector contract.

fix.application: Set in the deployed application configuration if downstream parsing needs the old timestamp.
fix.caveat: External LOG_DATEFORMAT_PATTERN, logging exclusions, JSON encoders and external logging files are unknown; inspect the real collector contract.

drifts.title: Legacy auto-configuration registration is ignored
drifts.new_behavior: Auto-configuration discovery uses the imports resource.
drifts.business_impact: An optional integration can disappear while the rest of the application starts.

detection.summary: A local spring.factories declares EnableAutoConfiguration entries.
detection.limitations: Optional auto-configurations can vanish silently; required missing beans may instead fail startup. Dependency JAR resources are not scanned. Existing imports must be compared class by class; this rule deliberately remains a review finding.

fix.application: Create that resource and list every legacy auto-configuration class, one fully qualified name per line; replace the example with your actual classes. Keep dual registration for 2.7 compatibility.
fix.caveat: Optional auto-configurations can vanish silently; required missing beans may instead fail startup. Dependency JAR resources are not scanned. Existing imports must be compared class by class; this rule deliberately remains a review finding.

drifts.title: RestTemplate loses Apache HttpClient 4 selection
drifts.old_behavior: Boot can select Apache HttpClient 4 automatically.
drifts.new_behavior: That dependency no longer selects an Apache client.
drifts.business_impact: Automatic client fallback can change connection pooling and request behavior.

detection.summary: HttpClient 4 dependency plus RestTemplateBuilder, without HttpClient 5.
detection.limitations: The fix restores the client family, not byte-for-byte HttpClient 4 semantics. Custom request factories can invalidate this signature. Direct HttpClient 4 factory constructors are compilation migrations and are not this silent case.

fix.application: Add the Boot-managed HttpClient 5 dependency to restore Apache-backed auto-selection. Port explicit HttpClient 4 timeouts, TLS and pool customizations separately.
fix.caveat: The fix restores the client family, not byte-for-byte HttpClient 4 semantics. Custom request factories can invalidate this signature. Direct HttpClient 4 factory constructors are compilation migrations and are not this silent case.

drifts.title: Default JMX endpoint exposure shrinks
drifts.old_behavior: JMX exposes all enabled actuator endpoints by default.
drifts.new_behavior: JMX exposes only health by default.
drifts.business_impact: JMX-based monitoring loses metrics or diagnostic operations.

detection.summary: Actuator and explicit JMX enablement without an exposure override.
detection.limitations: This is JMX exposure, not HTTP exposure. Restoring all JMX endpoints can reveal sensitive operations; an explicit allowlist is preferable where feasible.

fix.application: Set this to restore the old JMX exposure set, or enumerate the endpoint IDs used by your monitoring.
fix.caveat: This is JMX exposure, not HTTP exposure. Restoring all JMX endpoints can reveal sensitive operations; an explicit allowlist is preferable where feasible.

drifts.title: Actuator stops using application Jackson customization
drifts.old_behavior: Actuator JSON can use the application ObjectMapper.
drifts.new_behavior: Built-in endpoints use an isolated mapper.
drifts.business_impact: Consumers expecting custom JSON names or formats receive a different contract.

detection.summary: Actuator with an ObjectMapper/customizer or spring.jackson configuration.
detection.limitations: A mapper reference may be unrelated to Boot customization; determine which endpoint payload fields are actually affected. This is not a general Jackson default-change claim.

fix.application: Set this to let built-in actuator JSON use the application mapper again.
fix.caveat: A mapper reference may be unrelated to Boot customization; determine which endpoint payload fields are actually affected. This is not a general Jackson default-change claim.

drifts.title: Redis configuration under the old prefix is ignored
drifts.business_impact: A reachable default Redis can receive reads or writes in the wrong logical database.

detection.summary: Redis dependency and at least one old-prefix property in application configuration.
detection.limitations: If fallback Redis is unreachable, failure occurs at first connection instead. Values here are example values, never inferred production values. Custom RedisConnectionFactory beans or the temporary properties migrator can override binding.

fix.code:
# Preserve each original value while changing its key prefix.
# Example: spring.redis.database=4 becomes:
spring.data.redis.database=4
fix.application: Rename all spring.redis.* keys to spring.data.redis.* in every deployed property source; retain each original value.
fix.caveat: If fallback Redis is unreachable, failure occurs at first connection instead. Values here are example values, never inferred production values. Custom RedisConnectionFactory beans or the temporary properties migrator can override binding.

drifts.title: Metrics exporter configuration moves
drifts.business_impact: An ignored enablement or sampling setting changes monitoring behavior.

detection.summary: An old metrics exporter property is present with Actuator.
detection.limitations: This is a potential finding until the corresponding registry is known to be installed. New-prefix duplicates and properties-migrator behavior require review.

fix.code:
# Preserve the original value; this example restores disabled export.
management.prometheus.metrics.export.enabled=false
fix.application: Rewrite management.metrics.export.<product>.<suffix> as management.<product>.metrics.export.<suffix> for the exporter you actually use.
fix.caveat: This is a potential finding until the corresponding registry is known to be installed. New-prefix duplicates and properties-migrator behavior require review.

drifts.title: Custom authentication no longer persists automatically
drifts.old_behavior: The default persistence filter saves custom context changes between requests.
drifts.new_behavior: The default holder filter reads context; custom authentication must save it explicitly.
drifts.business_impact: A custom login succeeds for one request but the following request is anonymous.

detection.summary: Servlet Security plus custom SecurityContextHolder writes.
detection.limitations: Do not change a deliberately stateless API. A same-file saveContext call is not proof of correct control flow; review every custom authentication path and chain.

fix.code:
// Merge into the existing HttpSecurity chain before build().
http.securityContext(context -> context.requireExplicitSave(false));
fix.application: Use the migration opt-out in the existing SecurityFilterChain, or explicitly save the context through the configured SecurityContextRepository after authenticating.
fix.caveat: Do not change a deliberately stateless API. A same-file saveContext call is not proof of correct control flow; review every custom authentication path and chain.

drifts.title: Saved request lookup requires a continue parameter
drifts.old_behavior: Default saved-request matching may consult the session on every request.
drifts.new_behavior: Default matching is gated by the continue query parameter.
drifts.business_impact: Custom post-login navigation without that parameter can lose saved request restoration.

detection.summary: Servlet Security form login or request-cache customization without NullRequestCache.
detection.limitations: Standard saved-request login redirects normally include continue, so formLogin alone indicates review risk, not a broken login. The opt-out increases session reads.

fix.application: Install this request cache in the existing chain when a custom navigation contract cannot carry continue.
fix.caveat: Standard saved-request login redirects normally include continue, so formLogin alone indicates review risk, not a broken login. The opt-out increases session reads.

drifts.title: An implicit HQL join changes result shape
drifts.old_behavior: An HQL join without select returns object-array tuples of joined entities.
drifts.new_behavior: The same implicit select returns the root entity.
drifts.business_impact: Untyped result processing or serialization can silently lose joined columns.

detection.summary: Hibernate dependency and a literal HQL from/join query without an explicit select.
detection.limitations: Criteria, concatenated query strings and runtime-built HQL are not parsed. Typed consumers can fail at runtime instead of silently changing output. Business impact depends on result consumption.

fix.code: select c, o from Customer c join c.orders o
fix.application: Explicitly select the root and each joined alias in the legacy tuple order; substitute the actual entities and aliases from your query.
fix.caveat: Criteria, concatenated query strings and runtime-built HQL are not parsed. Typed consumers can fail at runtime instead of silently changing output. Business impact depends on result consumption.

drifts.title: Native Hibernate no longer copies criteria by default
drifts.old_behavior: Mutating criteria after createQuery does not change an already created Query.
drifts.new_behavior: Native bootstrap defaults to sharing the criteria tree; later mutations can affect Query.
drifts.business_impact: Reused criteria can change a query predicate and therefore the selected business records.

detection.summary: Criteria usage plus native buildSessionFactory bootstrap, not merely an EntityManager.
detection.limitations: Ordinary Boot JPA bootstrap already enables copying and is excluded. Static matching cannot prove that criteria are mutated after Query creation; inspect reuse order. The property can also be set explicitly false under JPA, a case this native-only detector does not cover.

fix.code:
// Apply to the native org.hibernate.cfg.Configuration before buildSessionFactory().
configuration.setProperty("hibernate.criteria.copy_tree", "true");
fix.application: Enable copying on the native Hibernate bootstrap configuration, or complete all mutations before creating each Query.
fix.caveat: Ordinary Boot JPA bootstrap already enables copying and is excluded. Static matching cannot prove that criteria are mutated after Query creation; inspect reuse order. The property can also be set explicitly false under JPA, a case this native-only detector does not cover.
